epinephrine_inh_croup.notes: Croup: 0.5 mL/kg of 1:1000 (1 mg/mL) ≤4 yr max 2.5 mL, >4 yr max 5 mL; observe 2-4 hours for rebound

clinical.warnings: observe 2-4 hr after dosing for rebound; concurrent steroid lowers admission rate

clinical.adverseEffects: increased heart rate, tremor, hypokalemia (high dose)
clinical.warnings: monitor K+ with repeated use; combine with ipratropium for acute asthma

clinical.use: acute asthma exacerbation (combined with a β-agonist)
clinical.adverseEffects: dry mouth, cough, rare acute angle-closure glaucoma (eye contact)
clinical.warnings: combine with a β-agonist within the first 24 hr of an exacerbation; do not use alone for an acute attack
recommended for age ≥6 yr; not suitable for acute attacks (slow onset)

meptin_tab.notes: dosed by weight group; age <6 yr, Meptin liquid is preferred

clinical.warnings: long-acting formulation; use nebulization for acute asthma

indications.label: Asthma loading
indications.frequency: Loading × 1, maintain 2 mg/kg/day (inpatient loading, 3-day take-home course)

clinical.use: croup, asthma, skin allergy, autoimmune disease
clinical.contraindications: active systemic infection, live vaccine within 24 hr
clinical.adverseEffects: short-term: hyperglycemia, mood changes; long-term: adrenal suppression, Cushingoid appearance, osteoporosis
clinical.warnings: croup/asthma short courses are usually 3 days; no taper needed for courses <14 days

indications.label: Asthma loading
indications.frequency: ST, maintain same total dose divided q6h

clinical.contraindications: live vaccine within 24 hr, systemic fungal infection
clinical.adverseEffects: short-term: hyperglycemia, HTN; long-term same as systemic corticosteroid effects
clinical.warnings: first choice IV/IM for an acute exacerbation; usually a single dose or ≤72 hr

aswell_syrup.notes: watch for EPS; may combine with diphenhydramine to prevent it

clinical.contraindications: GI obstruction / perforation, pheochromocytoma, history of tardive dyskinesia
clinical.adverseEffects: drowsiness, agitation, EPS (higher risk at young age)
clinical.warnings: age <1 yr high EPS risk; combine with diphenhydramine to prevent EPS; max 5-day course

warnings: EPS side effect — higher risk in children, may combine with diphenhydramine to prevent it

clinical.contraindications: GI obstruction / perforation, history of tardive dyskinesia
clinical.warnings: max 5-day course; treat acute EPS with diphenhydramine

clinical.adverseEffects: EPS (especially at young age), drowsiness, rare NMS
clinical.warnings: slow IV push (<2 min); combine with diphenhydramine to prevent EPS

clinical.contraindications: <2 yr, severe CNS depression, GI obstruction
clinical.warnings: contraindicated <2 yr; lower EPS risk than metoclopramide
simethicone is not absorbed; very high safety profile

clinical.use: adjunct for acute gastroenteritis, antibiotic-associated diarrhea prevention
clinical.contraindications: immunocompromised / central venous catheter (rare sepsis risk)
clinical.warnings: rare bacteremia in immunocompromised patients; use with caution in preterm infants
do not use in renal failure; max 2.1 g/day
short-term use; do not combine with other stimulant laxatives

smecta.notes: Under 1 yr: 1 pack/day; 1-2 yr: 2 pack/day; >2 yr: 3 pack/day. Space 1 hour apart from other medications.

clinical.warnings: space 1-2 hr apart from other oral medications (adsorbs other drugs)

smecta._review: source: Source resource name '藥丹' (TH/EN) is ambiguous/unverifiable (possibly a typo for 藥典 or a proper-noun reference tool); kept verbatim rather than guessing.

taita1.notes: D5W isotonic; commonly used fluid base for neonates/infants

clinical.warnings: calculate maintenance using the 4-2-1 rule; monitor blood glucose in infants

clinical.adverseEffects: fluid overload edema; prolonged hypotonic use requires monitoring for hyponatremia
clinical.warnings: recent guidelines favor isotonic fluids (such as D5NS); monitor Na if hypotonic fluid is used

taita5.notes: higher sugar content, prone to causing pain

clinical.warnings: higher sugar content, IV site prone to pain; caution in diabetes or stress hyperglycemia

morphine_inj.notes: controlled drug; watch for respiratory depression; halve the dose in neonates

contraindications.reason: high respiratory-depression risk in neonates; halve the dose

clinical.contraindications: active respiratory depression, paralytic ileus, acute phase of severe asthma
clinical.adverseEffects: respiratory depression, drowsiness, N/V, constipation, pruritus, histamine release
clinical.warnings: halve the dose in neonates; have naloxone ready for respiratory depression; slow IV push
clinical.breastfeeding: short-term use acceptable (watch for infant drowsiness)

fentanyl_inj.notes: controlled drug; rapid push risks chest wall rigidity; usually 1 mcg/kg for procedural sedation

clinical.adverseEffects: respiratory depression, drowsiness, chest wall rigidity (rapid push), low BP
clinical.warnings: pushing too fast may cause chest wall rigidity; have naloxone ready; slow IV over 1-2 min

warnings: hyperkalemia (contraindicated in burns / trauma / neuromuscular disease)

clinical.contraindications: 24 hr post-burn, upper/lower motor neuron injury, severe hyperkalemia, family history of malignant hyperthermia
clinical.adverseEffects: hyperkalemia, bradycardia (especially in children), myalgia, rare malignant hyperthermia
clinical.warnings: pediatric IV 1-2 mg/kg / IM 3-4 mg/kg; have atropine ready to prevent bradycardia, dantrolene to treat MH
